_doc: Seconds each step of .github/workflows/pages.yml may take, keyed 'job/step name'. tools/step_budgets.py check-run fails the build job's last step on a step over its budget or with no row; tools/test_step_budgets.sh fails on a step with no row, and on a step that reads the whole corpus without naming the cache it restores ('cache'), how it limits itself to what changed ('incremental'), or why it can do neither ('uncached'). Raise a budget only with the reason in the commit: a budget that moves with every slowdown catches nothing.

build/Check out.note: was 30. Two paths, measured over the last 100 runs of pages.yml (12 real build jobs): warm incremental fetch 9-12s (10 runs); and the store reset, where Check out finds the restored git store over 1500MB, drops .git and fetches from scratch, 91s and 94s (runs 40267913545, 40276271478). The store restarts at 335MB and grew to 1397MB and then 1660MB across the builds between resets, so the reset recurs about every 6th build (2 in 12): expected work, not runner variance, and it failed 2 of 12 builds against the old 30s. 150 = 1.6x the slowest reset seen (94s). The warm path is far under it (p99 12s); a warm-path regression now shows only as the step nearing 94s, which is the price of one row for both paths

build/Build the puzzle shims and reindex.note: 17-21s on warm shims and rows (runs 38378765553, 38385076152); 56-127s cold (127s in run 38390532020). Was 75, under that cold range: an edit to code the index rows reach (the format converter, run 38383021945) re-makes all ~51k rows by design and took 94s, so every such push went red for expected work

build/Draw the social cards.note: was 900: the card key hashed make_og_card.py's bytes, so any edit redrew all ~17k cards 600 a run (816s, run 38370347047). Now keyed on the card's rendered HTML: steady state is the cached list (~15-40s) plus the cards a push moved; worst case a code edit re-lists every row (~60s) and draws OG_LIMIT=120 cards at ~0.9s each. Was 240: with a cold row cache the re-list took 146s and the 120 cards 100s (246s, run 39653095057), as the corpus grew. Was 300: a scheduled run after a day of annotate-code edits re-listed every row in 223s on a warm row cache, then drew 120 cards in 102s (329s, run 40199706228)

build/Unpack the puzzle pages.note: untars the ~42k pages and the page store Restore the puzzle pages fetched as one file (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Generate the crawlable pages, shar.note: a quarter of the puzzle pages (--shard 0/4, by a hash of the id). A cold render of all of them was ~175s in one step, over the old 160s budget; a quarter is ~45s plus ~10s of startup. A code or data change re-renders every page (tools/page_cache.py's fingerprint); a puzzle push re-renders the pages whose inputs moved

build/Choose the build path.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
build/Choose the build path.note: the puzzle fast path's test (tools/ci_scope.py against the last deployed commit): a few gh api calls and one blobless fetch of that commit's trees. Run 39360349916 spent 37s of its 37s in that fetch (no checkout; the log is silent until it prints), a base 82 paths behind: the fetch of a ~54k-file tree set grows with how far the deployed commit is, so 30s was too tight; 60s still catches a regression

build/Generate the crawlable pages (puzz.note: replaces the 8 warming slices, 4 page shards and Assemble on a push that only changed puzzle files (Choose the build path). The 4 shards plus the assemble took ~87s warm (run 39236355785) of which ~40s was workers piping each reused page's blocks back; build_seo_pages --reuse-first checks the stored pages in the parent and renders only the rest. Budget is the assemble's, not raised

build/Assemble the crawlable pages.note: the serial tail (hub, listings, sitemaps, ~10s of CPU) after the shards, and the check that every page was rendered by exactly one of them. Replaces the one 160s step, Generate the crawlable pages

build/List the site.uncached: lists the published files by glob; it opens none of them
build/List the site.note: globs PUBLISH and writes the tar list. Was Stage the site, 45s: 23s hard-linking ~138k files into _site/ and 22s checking links (run 38385716791)

build/Start the site checks.uncached: starts the checks Wait for the site checks collects, and returns
build/Start the site checks.note: only starts the link check and the IndexNow hashing in the background; their time shows in Wait for the site checks

build/Upload the site.note: 39s at deflate level 1 (run 38378765553), 65s at level 6; stored (level 0) 18s (run 38380967725)

build/Wait for the site checks.uncached: the link check reads every published page (stage_site.py --check, across the cores) and IndexNow hashes them; they run beside Archive and Upload, so this is only what is left over
build/Wait for the site checks.note: was the check half of Stage the site (22s) plus List the changed pages (8s), in series in front of the upload

build/Wait for the annotation check.note: zero unless validate is still running when the build is ready, which only a full check does: validate then takes ~345s and the build reaches this step at ~190s since the cached checkout (124s in run 38380967725). Was 120 when the build was slower; covers a full check at its 300s budget. 219s in run 38636406433 (daily full check); 330 is 1.5x that

build/Deploy to Pages.note: GitHub side: 69-134s (134s in run 38391832453, same artifact) for the 2.5GB, ~138k-file artifact (runs 38385076152, 38385716791, 38383021945); scales with what is shipped, not with what changed

build/Pack the puzzle shims.note: tars puzzles/*.js, *.js.gz and shims.gz.json for Save the puzzle shims (tools/cache_tar.sh). Took 16-30s over the 7 builds before 10-22 (24s turned run 39811022168 red at the old 20s); grows with the corpus

build/Pack the puzzle pages.note: runs only when Save the puzzle pages does; tars the pages for it (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Save the puzzle pages.note: runs only after a render of over 2000 pages (a code change, a cold cache)

scope/Check out.note: depth 1, blob:none, sparse to tools: a few seconds

scope/Decide whether this run deploys.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
scope/Decide whether this run deploys.note: a puzzle-only push stops here and in validate (about a minute); the next scheduled tick deploys it. One gh api call for the live site's commit (tools/last_deploy.py), one blobless fetch of it, the diff

validate/Check out.note: already depth 1, blob:none, sparse to tools + .github/workflows; still 65s and 74s (runs 38636406433, 38635950789) as the tools tree grew. 1.5x the observed 74s

validate/Choose what to check.note: a full check fetches the whole tree here, in four streams; the diff and the scope are a few seconds. Was 75: full checks took 67-89s on 2026-10-22 (89s in run 39799670301, 76s in the red run 39796038374); 110 is 1.2x the 89s

validate/Check every annotation, shard 1.note: a sixth of the puzzles (--shard 0/6, by a hash of the id). The one full-check step took ~315s against its 300s budget on 2026-10-17 (profile flat: rules and corpus both grew), so it is split rather than the budget raised. The step scales with the corpus divided by the shard count: add shards, never seconds. Four shards then took 191-207s each in full builds on 2026-10-23 (runs 40039432205, 40039600729, 40039778370, 40040262106, 40040366466; 176-178s in 40039911558), over the 190 budget in the red ones and steady rather than one loaded runner, so it is now six shards: 4/6 of ~200s is ~133s expected, 190 is 1.4x that
validate/Check every annotation, shard 1.uncached: the nightly and rule-change full check, spread across the runner's cores (validate_annotations.check_all); its budget is the alarm that the shards need splitting again

validate/Check the changed annotations.incremental: only the puzzle files changed since the last successfully deployed commit (Choose what to check)
